rules.name: Consumer Duty — Ongoing Fair Value Assessment
rules.source_legislation: FCA Consumer Duty (PS22/9), effective 31 July 2023 (open book) and 31 July 2024 (closed book)
rules.description: The board must receive an annual attestation that all retail products — including current accounts, savings, overdrafts, personal loans, and packaged accounts — deliver fair value to their target market. The assessment must cover price/value, consumer understanding, consumer support, and products and services outcomes. Remedial action plans must be documented and tracked where gaps are identified.
disclosure_obligations: Annual board Consumer Duty attestation published in board minutes
Fair value assessment summary provided to FCA upon supervisory request
Product-level cost and benefit summary disclosed in standardised terms and conditions
Evidence of customer outcome monitoring retained for FCA review for minimum 5 years
constraints: Products found to deliver poor value must be withdrawn or restructured within a documented remediation timeline
Closed-book products must also be assessed — no grandfather exemption from July 2024
Marketing and communications must not mislead customers about price or features

rules.name: FSCS Deposit Protection — Eligible Deposits Limit
rules.source_legislation: PRA Rulebook — Depositor Protection; Financial Services Compensation Scheme (FSCS) rules
rules.description: All retail deposits up to £85,000 per eligible depositor per authorised firm must be protected under FSCS and clearly communicated at account opening and annually. Temporary high balance protection of up to £1m applies for 6 months following qualifying life events (home sale, divorce settlement, etc.). The bank must ensure FSCS information is displayed on all deposit product communications and maintain a depositor data file (Single Customer View) that can be extracted within 24 hours of a request from the FSCS.
disclosure_obligations: FSCS information sheet and exclusions list provided at account opening and annually
Temporary High Balance protection notification to eligible customers at point of qualifying deposit
Single Customer View file available to FSCS within 24 hours of a payout trigger
FSCS levy contribution reported annually to PRA
constraints: Maximum FSCS coverage per eligible depositor is £85,000 (standard) or £1,000,000 (temporary high balance, time-limited to 6 months)
Single Customer View system must be tested annually with PRA
Deposits in joint accounts count as £85,000 per account holder

rules.name: Overdraft Pricing — Single Annual Percentage Rate
rules.source_legislation: FCA PS19/16 (Overdraft Reforms), effective April 2020; FCA CONC 5A
rules.description: All authorised overdraft products must be priced using a single Annual Percentage Rate (APR). Fixed daily or monthly fees for overdraft usage are prohibited. The same APR must apply to arranged and unarranged overdrafts. The bank must conduct affordability assessments before granting or significantly increasing overdraft facilities, and must proactively identify and support customers in persistent debt.
disclosure_obligations: APR displayed prominently on all overdraft product pages, statements, and app interfaces
Pre-overdraft usage warning message when customer is about to enter overdraft (via app/SMS)
Annual overdraft interest cost summary in customer statements
Persistent debt letter at 18-month trigger point; suspension of facility at 36 months if not resolved
constraints: No fixed daily or monthly overdraft fees permitted
Unarranged overdraft rate cannot exceed the arranged overdraft APR
Persistent debt customers (paying more in charges than principal over 18 months) must receive intervention communication
Overdraft facility must be suspended for persistent debt customers if no resolution after 36 months

rules.name: Strong Customer Authentication (SCA) for Online Banking and Payments
rules.source_legislation: Payment Services Regulations 2017 (PSR 2017) Reg. 100; FCA RTS on SCA; OBIE SCA standards
rules.description: The bank must apply Strong Customer Authentication whenever a retail customer accesses their payment account online, initiates an electronic payment transaction, or carries out any action through a remote channel that may imply a risk of payment fraud or other abuses. SCA requires at least two independent elements from: knowledge (something only the user knows), possession (something only the user has), and inherence (something the user is). Exemptions (low-value, trusted beneficiary, low-risk transaction) must be monitored for fraud rate thresholds.
approval_chain: Head of Fraud and Financial Crime
disclosure_obligations: SCA method options disclosed to customers at onboarding and on-demand
Exemption usage rates reported to FCA quarterly under PSR 2017 monitoring
Fraud rates on SCA-exempt transactions monitored and escalated if thresholds breached
constraints: SCA must be applied to all online account access at least every 90 days (or session-by-session for higher-risk)
Low-value payment exemption limited to transactions under £30; aggregate cap £100 or 5 consecutive transactions
If fraud rate on a specific exemption type exceeds EBA reference thresholds, exemption must be suspended
Biometric authentication data must not be shared with third parties without explicit customer consent

rules.name: BNPL Regulation — Affordability and CONC Compliance
rules.source_legislation: Financial Services and Markets Act 2000 (Credit Agreements) (Amendment) Order (expected 2025–2026); FCA CONC extension to BNPL
rules.description: Following the incoming extension of the Consumer Credit Act and FCA CONC to Buy Now Pay Later products, the bank's any instalment credit or deferred payment product offered at point-of-sale will require full affordability assessments, right-to-withdraw disclosures, regulated credit agreements, and access to the Financial Ombudsman Service. Products must be assessed against Consumer Duty fair value requirements.
disclosure_obligations: Pre-contractual credit information (SECCI) in FCA-prescribed format
APR disclosed before credit agreement execution
14-day right-to-withdraw notice included in credit agreement
FOS jurisdiction disclosed in terms and conditions
constraints: Affordability assessment required before each instalment credit agreement is entered
Maximum deferred payment period subject to FCA CONC rules once enacted
Must be FCA authorised for consumer credit if offering BNPL as principal (not agent)

rules.name: Open Finance — Smart Data Scheme Participation
rules.source_legislation: Data (Use and Access) Act 2025; FCA Smart Data Scheme Rules (anticipated 2026–2027)
rules.description: The Data (Use and Access) Act 2025 creates the legislative basis for Smart Data schemes beyond Open Banking, extending data portability obligations to mortgage, savings, pensions, and insurance data. Once FCA makes scheme rules, the bank must provide standardised APIs granting eligible third parties access to customer data across all in-scope product lines, with customer consent. Participation will be mandatory for banks above the scheme threshold.
approval_chain: Head of Open Banking and Data
disclosure_obligations: Customer-facing consent dashboard showing all active data-sharing consents across product lines
Annual Smart Data participation report to FCA
Privacy notices updated to reflect Smart Data scheme data flows
constraints: Data must be provided in FCA-mandated standardised format within prescribed latency
Customer data may only be shared pursuant to valid, recorded customer consent
Bank must not discriminate against customers who share data with third parties
